subject.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): add timeouts to model discovery requests

question: Should Amazon Bedrock discovery enforce a fixed 30-second per-request cutoff without real provider latency evidence?
rationale: The deadline prevents indefinite setup and refresh waits but can also discard legitimate slow control-plane responses, so the cutoff needs provider-owner acceptance or calibrated evidence.

options.title: Require calibrated proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until redacted live Bedrock or controlled real-network evidence demonstrates bounded stall recovery and an unaffected normal successful discovery.

options.title: Accept bounded degradation
options.body: Merge with explicit provider-owner acceptance that responses exceeding 30 seconds may fall back to an empty or partial discovered catalog.

recommendation.title: Require calibrated proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until redacted live Bedrock or controlled real-network evidence demonstrates bounded stall recovery and an unaffected normal successful discovery.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the inference-profile discovery path most directly affected by the new deadline.
